claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Firstly, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 20 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 20 years old, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether he is in approved education or training. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and stays in approved education or training.

Could you tell me if Alex is currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, a BTEC, or other non-advanced education)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not studying at the moment. He finished school a while back and he's just been working part-time and figuring out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, it appears you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

- Child Benefit is normally available for children **under 16**, or for those **under 20** who remain in **approved education or training**.
- Since Alex is **20 years old** and is **not in approved education or training**, he no longer meets the age and education requirements for Child Benefit.

Additionally, the fact that Alex is working (even part-time) would also affect eligibility, as Child Benefit stops if a child works 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

Before I make my final determination, could you just confirm:
1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week?

This will help me provide you with a complete assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, I do live in the UK - we're in Manchester. 

And no, Alex isn't working that much - he just does a few shifts here and there at a local shop, definitely not 24 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming those details.

Even though you live in the UK and Alex works fewer than 24 hours per week, unfortunately the key issue is Alex's age and education status:

- Alex is **20 years old**
- He is **not in approved education or training**

Child Benefit can only be claimed for children who are either:
- Under 16, **or**
- Under 20 **and** in approved education or training

Since Alex is already 20 and not in approved education or training, he no longer qualifies for Child Benefit regardless of his work hours.

Let me provide you with my final assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm sorry to say that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Summary:**

| Child | Eligible? | Reason |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| Alex | No | At 20 years old and not in approved education or training, Alex exceeds the age eligibility requirements for Child Benefit. |

**Key points:**
- Child Benefit is available for children under 16, or those under 20 who are in approved education or training
- Since Alex is 20 and not studying, he no longer qualifies
- His part-time work status doesn't affect this outcome as the primary issue is his age and education status

I understand this may not be the news you were hoping for. If you have any other questions or if Alex's circumstances change (for example, if he decides to go back into approved education before turning 20 - though he's already 20), please don't hesitate to ask.
